import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' to datetime for better handling
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Aggregate total sales by date
daily_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('date').sum().reset_index()

# Create a line plot for total sales over time
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
sns.lineplot(data=daily_sales, x='date', y='total', marker='o')

# Adding titles and labels
plt.title('Daily Coffee Sales Over Time', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Load the dataset
coffee_sales = pd.read_csv('data/coffee_sales.csv')

# Convert 'date' to datetime for better handling
coffee_sales['date'] = pd.to_datetime(coffee_sales['date'])

# Aggregate total sales by date
daily_sales = coffee_sales.groupby('date').sum().reset_index()

# Create a line plot for total sales over time
plt.figure(figsize=(14, 7))
sns.lineplot(data=daily_sales, x='date', y='total', marker='o')

# Adding titles and labels
plt.title('Daily Coffee Sales Over Time', fontsize=16)
plt.xlabel('Date', fontsize=14)
plt.ylabel('Total Sales ($)', fontsize=14)
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.grid(True)

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
